title: Build RESTful backend services on Linux platforms
description: Develop, run, and test backend services using Python or Java that expose REST APIs. Configure the service in a Linux or Ubuntu environment and demonstrate correct request handling, error responses, and basic integration behavior.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to trace bugs, follow interface specifications accurately, and document endpoints so other developers can integrate with the service.
rationale: The title matches the strongest recurring backend signals in the cluster: Python, Java, API, REST, Linux, and Ubuntu. A learner can prove mastery by implementing a small service, documenting endpoints, testing responses, and deploying it locally on Linux. The competency is concrete enough for D3 or D4 assessment because it requires selecting language, runtime, and interface design choices. It is distinct from the mobile and data competencies because the main product is a server-side API service rather than a client UI or streaming pipeline.
future_relevance: Stable: REST APIs, Linux deployment, Python, and Java remain core foundations for enterprise and platform software.

title: Integrate data streaming and AI platform components
description: Configure and use platform components such as Kafka, Spark, Redis, and AI platforms to move, process, or cache application data. Demonstrate a small pipeline or integration that ingests data, transforms or routes it, and makes results available to another service.
soft_skills_description: Learners must understand how data moves between components, diagnose bottlenecks or failures, and choose suitable integration patterns.
rationale: Kafka, Spark, Redis, AI platforms, and Python indicate a platform-oriented data integration theme. A learner can demonstrate mastery by building a small data flow, using Redis for fast access, Kafka for messaging, or Spark/Python for processing. The competency is broader than a single tool but still anchored in common platform components found in job postings. It is distinct from backend API work because the main emphasis is data movement, processing, caching, and AI-platform integration rather than endpoint implementation.
future_relevance: Emerging: data streaming, caching, and AI platform integration are becoming more important as applications embed real-time and AI-enabled features.

title: Build SQL and Power BI analytics solutions for accounting data
description: Prepare, query, model, and visualize business or accounting data using SQL and Power BI. Create dashboards or analytical tools that support operational reporting and basic performance optimization.
soft_skills_description: Learners must interpret numeric results carefully, validate outputs against business rules, and present findings in ways that non-technical users can understand.
rationale: The included skills point to practical business-intelligence work using SQL, Power BI, analytics, and accounting-domain data. A learner can prove mastery by transforming sample accounting records, writing SQL queries, and publishing a Power BI dashboard with useful measures and filters. Optimization fits as improving query, model, or dashboard performance. This competency is separate from requirements work because the assessed artifact is a working analytical product.
future_relevance: Emerging: demand for self-service BI, SQL literacy, and finance-oriented analytics continues to grow across software and business teams.

title: Support cloud-enabled infrastructure and delivery pipelines
description: Analyze system infrastructure needs, identify technical problems, and support deployment workflows using PaaS and CI/CD concepts. Select standard design and troubleshooting approaches for reliable application delivery.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to isolate technical causes, communicate deployment issues clearly, and work with developers or operations staff to restore reliable delivery.
rationale: The skills combine infrastructure knowledge, PaaS, CI/CD, system analysis, troubleshooting, and basic system design. A learner can demonstrate mastery by mapping an application deployment architecture, configuring a simple pipeline scenario, and diagnosing a failed build or deployment case. The competency is not a full DevOps specialization, but it prepares learners to participate in modern delivery environments. It is distinct from BI and documentation because the focus is operational reliability and deployment flow.
future_relevance: Emerging: cloud platforms and CI/CD pipelines are increasingly standard in software delivery, even for entry and diploma-level roles.

title: Analyze business requirements and document solution specifications
description: Elicit, interpret, and organize software or data-system requirements into clear specifications, decision records, and user-facing documentation. Use collaborative documentation tools to maintain traceability between requirements, system behavior, and project deliverables.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to ask precise questions, reconcile different stakeholder needs, and write documentation that other team members can reliably use.
rationale: The title reflects the strong overlap among requirements gathering, business analysis, and documentation skills. A learner can demonstrate mastery by producing a requirements brief, acceptance criteria, process notes, and maintained Confluence-style documentation for a small system. Project management is included only as coordination around requirements and deliverables. This is distinct from analytics or infrastructure work because the primary output is an agreed specification and documentation set.
future_relevance: Stable: requirements analysis and maintainable documentation remain essential as software teams adopt more tools and automation.

title: Operate secure and observable software services
description: Apply basic cybersecurity and observability practices to monitor, diagnose, and support software services. Use workflow or service-management tools such as Jira and ServiceNow to track incidents, changes, and remediation tasks.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to coordinate with teammates, report incidents clearly, and follow agreed procedures when handling operational or security issues.
rationale: Observability, cybersecurity, ServiceNow, Jira, and Linux form an operations-focused competency around running services safely and reliably. Mastery can be shown by instrumenting logs or metrics, identifying a security or reliability issue, and recording the response in an issue or service-management workflow. The competency fits vocational curricula because learners can practice standard procedures while also making basic diagnostic decisions. It is distinct from building software because assessment centers on monitoring, incident handling, and operational control.
future_relevance: Emerging: observability and cybersecurity are increasing in importance as software systems become more distributed and risk-sensitive.

title: Analyze data and build basic machine learning models
description: Prepare datasets, perform exploratory data analysis, select an appropriate machine learning approach, and train a basic model for a defined prediction or classification task. Evaluate results using suitable metrics and communicate limitations clearly.
soft_skills_description: Learners must reason from data, check assumptions carefully, and explain results and limitations to technical or non-technical stakeholders.
rationale: The title reflects the strongest signals in the cluster: machine learning, AI/ML, and data analysis. A learner can demonstrate mastery by cleaning a dataset, training a supervised model, evaluating accuracy or error, and explaining model behavior. This is distinct from the generative AI competency because it focuses on conventional model-building workflows rather than prompt-based or foundation-model applications. It also differs from the vision/robotics competency because the task can use tabular or general datasets without perception hardware.
future_relevance: Stable to Emerging: machine learning remains a core software and data capability while tooling continues to evolve rapidly.

title: Deploy and operate cloud infrastructure on AWS and Azure
description: Provision basic compute, storage, networking, and managed services in AWS and Azure using standard procedures. Monitor service status, apply configuration changes, and document the deployed cloud environment for operational handover.
soft_skills_description: Learners need accuracy when configuring resources, clear documentation for handover, and structured troubleshooting when cloud services do not behave as expected.
rationale: The title directly reflects the cluster emphasis on AWS, Azure, cloud infrastructure, and cloud services. A learner could demonstrate mastery by deploying a small cloud environment, configuring core services, and explaining the purpose of each component. Assessment can include screenshots, configuration records, cost-aware service choices, and basic troubleshooting logs. It is distinct from the DevOps competency because the focus is on operating cloud resources rather than automating software delivery pipelines.
future_relevance: Stable, because AWS and Azure remain dominant platforms and cloud infrastructure operation is a core requirement across software teams.

title: Model financial workflows for software applications
description: Analyze basic finance, financial services, planning, and reporting requirements and translate them into software data fields, calculations, and user workflows. Produce simple specifications or prototypes for reports, budgets, transaction summaries, or fintech service features.
soft_skills_description: Learners must handle financial data carefully, reason through calculations and reporting rules, and recognize the sensitivity of financial information.
rationale: The title matches the finance-oriented items because it focuses on converting financial domain knowledge into implementable software behavior. A learner could demonstrate mastery by defining entities such as accounts, transactions, budgets, and reports, then validating sample calculations or report outputs. The inclusion of fintech and financial services keeps the competency relevant to digital products, not only accounting theory. It is distinct from commerce and supply-chain competencies because the main assessment evidence is financial logic, reporting, and planning workflows.
future_relevance: Emerging because fintech, embedded finance, and automated reporting continue to expand demand for developers who understand financial workflows.

title: Develop cross-platform client applications
description: Create simple user-facing applications or front-end modules using React and mobile platform concepts for Android and iOS. Connect the client to an API and demonstrate responsive interaction, navigation, and basic data display.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to interpret user needs, explain interface choices, and refine the application after testing or feedback.
rationale: The included skills point to client-side development across web and mobile contexts: React for web UI and Android/iOS for mobile platforms. Mastery can be shown through a working interface that consumes an API, handles user input, and displays returned data. This competency is assessable without requiring full native mobile specialization because the focus is client integration and platform awareness. It is separate from backend services because learners are evaluated on user interaction, presentation, and client behavior rather than server design.
future_relevance: Stable: React and mobile platform knowledge remain widely used, while cross-platform delivery continues to be important for software products.

title: Automate AI-enabled software workflows
description: Design and implement scripts, integrations, or low-code services that automate recurring software or business workflows. Use AI-enabled workflow concepts where appropriate to improve routing, summarization, classification, or task handoff while maintaining human review points.
soft_skills_description: Learners must communicate with process owners, identify repetitive steps accurately, and validate that automation improves work without creating hidden failure points.
rationale: The title reflects the cluster items centered on automation and AI-enabled workflows. A learner could demonstrate mastery by mapping a manual workflow, selecting automation points, implementing the workflow, and testing error handling. The AI aspect is included only where it supports concrete workflow tasks rather than as a general AI competency. It is distinct from architecture and distributed systems because the focus is on improving task execution and process flow, not designing system-wide structure or operating infrastructure.
future_relevance: Emerging, because organizations increasingly expect software teams to embed AI-assisted automation into routine workflows.

title: Deploy containerized applications with Docker and Kubernetes
description: Build and run application containers using Docker, then deploy and manage them in a Kubernetes environment. Learners configure basic workloads, expose services, and verify application health using standard operational procedures.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to trace deployment issues methodically, record configuration decisions, and communicate operational status to teammates.
rationale: Docker and Kubernetes form a coherent deployment competency because containers are commonly built before being orchestrated in clusters. Mastery can be demonstrated by packaging an application in a Docker image, deploying it to Kubernetes, and validating that the service runs correctly. Learners can also show basic troubleshooting by inspecting logs, pods, and service status. It is distinct from cloud provisioning because the focus is application runtime operations rather than creating cloud infrastructure resources.
future_relevance: Stable: containerization and Kubernetes remain widely used for scalable application deployment, though tooling around them continues to evolve.
